zones.label: Name It
zones.summary: Naming an emotion can make the experience easier to understand.
facts: More than one feeling can be present.
Use language that fits the person.

zones.label: Body Signals
zones.summary: Notice breathing, tension, energy, temperature, stomach, and movement cues.
facts: Persistent symptoms may need health assessment.

zones.label: Pause
zones.summary: Create a small gap before acting when it is safe.
facts: A pause may be one breath, a step back, or more time.
Urgent danger calls for immediate safety action.

zones.label: Choose a Tool
zones.summary: Select from breathing, movement, art, music, nature, grounding, or rest.
facts: Match the strategy to the situation and culture.

zones.label: Connect
zones.summary: Co-regulation and support can help when feelings are intense.
facts: Ask a trusted person to listen or stay nearby.
Professional help is appropriate when distress disrupts life or safety.

zones.label: Reflect
zones.summary: Review what triggered the feeling and what helped afterward.
facts: Use learning to adjust the plan.
